definition: Thin film coating applies a thin layer of material to a surface to change properties such as optical behavior, wear, adhesion, or conductivity.
example: An optical engineer applies and evaluates an antireflection coating on a lens.

definition: Third party risk management identifies, assesses, monitors, and treats risks arising from suppliers, partners, contractors, or other external relationships.
example: An organization checks a cloud vendor's recovery commitments and reviews its performance annually.

definition: Threading forms a helical ridge or groove on an internal or external surface so parts can engage with matching threads.
example: A machinist verifies that a tapped hole accepts the specified fastener and meets its thread gauge requirements.

definition: Threat modeling systematically examines an asset or system's design, trust boundaries, and plausible adverse events to prioritize defenses.
example: A team diagrams who can access a document store and checks whether its authorization rules match the stated trust boundaries.

definition: Three.js is a JavaScript library that abstracts browser graphics rendering to create interactive three-dimensional scenes.
example: A developer creates a rotatable 3D preview of a product for a web page.

definition: A thyroid biopsy collects cells or tissue from the thyroid for microscopic or other diagnostic evaluation.
example: A clinician reviews a biopsy report to help characterize a thyroid nodule.

definition: Thyroid ultrasound uses sound waves to image the thyroid gland and assess features such as its size and nodules.
example: A clinician compares ultrasound measurements from two examinations to assess whether a nodule has changed.

definition: TIBCO ActiveMatrix is a suite of enterprise middleware products for integrating applications and building, deploying, or managing services and processes.
example: An integration team connects two enterprise applications and monitors exchanges through an ActiveMatrix product.
sense_note: The label names a product family; the exact component is unspecified.

definition: TIBCO Designer is a graphical development environment used in legacy TIBCO products to configure integration resources and processes.
example: A maintainer opens a historical BusinessWorks project to trace where its message mappings are defined.
sense_note: Legacy design tooling; verify product and version.

definition: TIBCO Enterprise Message Service is enterprise messaging middleware that implements Java Message Service APIs and supports queues and topics.
example: An order service publishes a message to a queue for later processing by another application.

definition: TIBCO iProcess Suite is business process management software for defining, executing, and tracking workflows that may include assigned human work.
example: An operations team routes applications to reviewers and reports where cases are waiting.

definition: Spotfire is a visual analytics platform for interactively exploring data and developing analyses or dashboards.
example: An engineer compares sensor readings by equipment type and filters the views to inspect a suspected trend.

definition: The Time Protocol is a simple network protocol that returns a binary count of seconds since the beginning of 1900 for time retrieval.
example: A network historian identifies the Time Protocol in an archived system and distinguishes it from NTP.
sense_note: Interpreted as the specific RFC 868 protocol, not network time protocols in general.

definition: TinyDB is a lightweight Python document database that commonly stores records in a local JSON file.
example: A small command-line utility keeps a local set of bookmarked items and queries their tags.
sense_note: Interpreted as the Python library; TinyDB also names a wireless sensor network query system.

definition: Tire balancing corrects uneven wheel-assembly mass distribution, while rotation periodically changes tire positions to help distribute wear.
example: A shop corrects a measured wheel imbalance and rotates the tires according to the vehicle's recommended pattern.

definition: TOGAF is an enterprise architecture framework and methodology for developing, managing, and governing architecture aligned to organizational goals.
example: An architecture team uses the framework to describe a target operating model and plan the transition from current systems.

definition: TokuDB was a MySQL-compatible storage engine designed for high insertion rates using fractal tree indexes and compression.
example: A database engineer plans a migration away from TokuDB while checking how its indexes and compression affect the workload.
sense_note: Historical storage engine; availability varies by product version.

definition: Agent tool use is the selection and invocation of external functions by an agent, followed by interpretation of their results within defined permissions and task constraints.
example: An assistant calls an approved calendar lookup and checks returned availability before suggesting meeting times.

definition: Toon Boom is a family of animation and storyboard software used to plan and produce digital animated productions.
example: An animator uses Toon Boom Harmony to rig a character and revise its poses across a shot.
sense_note: The label may denote the vendor or one of several products.

definition: TopSolid is a suite of computer-aided design and manufacturing tools for designing parts, assemblies, and manufacturing processes.
example: A manufacturer uses TopSolid to model a fixture and prepare compatible machining operations.

definition: Torch is an older Lua-based scientific computing and machine learning framework with tensor and neural network libraries.
example: A researcher examines an archived Lua Torch model to understand its layer definitions before porting it.
sense_note: Distinguish original Torch, often called Torch7, from Python-based PyTorch unless the source equates the label.

definition: Tourism management plans and operates visitor services and destinations while considering demand, service quality, sustainability, and local impacts.
example: A destination manager adds off-season activities and monitors whether demand shifts away from congested peak weeks.

definition: Track and trace records the identity, movement, and history of items or consignments so their current state and prior locations can be established.
example: A food distributor follows a batch identifier from supplier receipt through shipments to several stores.
sense_note: Broad supply-chain sense; other domains may use dedicated variants.

definition: TrackWise is quality management software used to manage regulated or controlled processes such as deviations, audits, and corrective actions.
example: A manufacturer logs a deviation and links it to a corrective action and effectiveness check.
sense_note: Verify edition where cloud and legacy implementations differ.

definition: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System is an airborne system that monitors nearby transponder-equipped aircraft and alerts crews to potential conflicts, with applicable versions providing resolution advisories.
example: A flight training simulator demonstrates how a crew distinguishes a traffic advisory from a resolution advisory.

definition: Traffic collision reconstruction uses physical evidence and engineering analysis to estimate the sequence and dynamics of a road crash.
example: A reconstruction specialist compares vehicle damage, scene measurements, and recordings to assess competing accounts of a collision.

definition: A training and development needs assessment identifies performance or capability gaps and determines whether training or another intervention would address them.
example: An evaluator separates unfamiliarity with a new process from delays caused by an unavailable tool before recommending training.

definition: Training material development creates instructional content, practice opportunities, and assessment materials aligned with learning objectives and audience needs.
example: A trainer builds a job aid, worked example, and exercise for a new warehouse receiving process.

definition: The Trans-Proteomic Pipeline is a software suite for processing, validating, and interpreting mass-spectrometry evidence in proteomics.
example: A researcher uses pipeline reports to compare confidence in peptide identifications across archived datasets.

definition: Transaction monitoring reviews transactions and patterns against rules, models, or expectations to identify activity requiring investigation.
example: A financial compliance analyst reviews why a flagged set of account transfers departed from expected activity.
sense_note: Often financial crime or fraud monitoring, but operational transaction monitoring is also possible.

definition: Transient expression is the temporary production of a gene product in cells without establishing stable long-term expression in the population.
example: A student distinguishes a short-lived expression signal in a research report from evidence of a stable cell line.

definition: Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy is a structured psychotherapy that combines trauma-focused and cognitive behavioral methods to address trauma-related symptoms, commonly in children and adolescents and with caregiver involvement when appropriate.
example: A trained clinician works with a child and caregiver within an individualized trauma recovery plan.
sense_note: Capitalized TF-CBT usually refers to a specific manualized model, not all trauma-focused CBT approaches.

definition: Travel coordination organizes transportation, accommodation, timing, documentation, and changes around travelers' needs and constraints.
example: A coordinator rebooks an accessible transfer after a flight schedule changes.

definition: Treatment planning translates findings and patient goals into a proposed sequence of care actions, monitoring, and reassessment.
example: A rehabilitation team agrees with a patient on functional goals and how recovery will be measured.
sense_note: The broad label does not specify a clinical discipline.

definition: A treemap depicts hierarchical or grouped data as nested rectangles whose areas represent a selected quantity.
example: A financial dashboard shows department budgets as rectangles sized by expenditure.

definition: A trendline is a fitted or smoothed line that summarizes the predominant direction or pattern in plotted observations.
example: An analyst overlays a fitted line on monthly sales and inspects where individual months depart from it.

definition: TV production coordinates the preparation, recording, and postproduction of content intended for television distribution.
example: A production team schedules interviews, records footage, and edits it into a timed documentary episode.

definition: Twitch is a livestreaming platform that combines broadcast video with viewer interaction such as live chat.
example: A creator streams a demonstration and appoints moderators to help manage the audience chat.

definition: Twitter advertising is the use of paid placements and campaign tools on the service historically named Twitter to reach defined audiences.
example: A campaign manager compares the cost per registration of two promoted posts.
sense_note: Platform later branded X; historical tools and present offerings may differ.

definition: Twitter marketing uses content, community interaction, and sometimes paid promotion to achieve communication goals on the service historically named Twitter.
example: A nonprofit schedules public updates and tracks which posts lead to event signups.
sense_note: Platform later branded X; the label does not imply paid advertising only.
